decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to the left basket, lifting and tipping the gripper downward with small continuous increments; right arm stays home.
Move above the back egg in the left basket while continuing the downward wrist tilt. Keep clearance above the rim.
Align vertically over the back egg and descend slowly with the left gripper open; estimated link-to-grasp offset is about 14 cm.
Fine-align and close the left jaws around the back egg, then perform a short retention-test lift. Grasp success remains visual.
Lift the first egg clear of the basket with the gripper closed, then begin moving toward the holder while angling the fingers inward.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the back-left cup, keeping the left EE on its own side and lowering only after clearing the basket.
Lower the first egg into the back-left cup with a slight rightward alignment correction; keep closed until it is seated.
Descent showed a substantial residual. Withdraw slightly toward the front and re-angle the held egg for a less crowded approach to the cup.
With the wrist clear and egg retained, lower along the front-angled approach toward the back-left socket.
Seat the egg with a small final alignment, open over the back-left cup, and lift away to check placement visually.
The first egg is visible in its cup. Retract up and left toward the remaining eggs, restoring a near-vertical grasp orientation.
Approach the leftmost remaining egg from above with open jaws, descending conservatively and centering from the head and wrist views.
Finish the short descent around the centered second egg, close fully, and lift a few centimeters to check retention.
Lift the second egg clear, checking visible retention, and begin a front-angled transfer toward the holder's front-left cup.
Move the held second egg toward the front-left socket, angling the wrist from the front to avoid the raised lid and maintaining a closed grip.
The second egg slipped and is visible in front of the holder. Open the left jaws and make a slow, more vertical recovery approach.
The loose egg rolled forward into the right-side workspace. Clear the left arm back toward the basket and start a right-arm recovery approach while the egg settles.
Bring the right gripper above the settled loose egg while the left aligns over a remaining basket egg. Maintain separated workspaces and gradual wrist rotations.
Align both open grippers above their respective eggs and lower slowly; the right approaches the loose egg at the front, while the left stays over the basket.
Correct the left egg's shifted position and the right egg's small lateral offset, close each gripper, then make short vertical retention-test lifts.
Lift the left egg vertically. The right grasp appears shallow, so reopen and re-center slightly forward and lower before retrying closure.
Transfer the left egg without rotating it toward the front-left cup. Reattempt the shallow right grasp farther forward and lower, keeping the arms separated.
Move the held left egg away from the lid and use a front-angled approach. Recenter the right jaws over the loose egg before another short grasp test.
Keep both eggs closed in the jaws. Lift the recovered right egg vertically while moving the left egg away from the lid and down toward the front-left cup.
The left egg is no longer between the fingers; clear that arm and observe where it settles. Carry the retained right egg forward toward the front-right cup without wrist rotation.
Align the retained right egg above the front-right socket, lowering slowly without changing its grasp orientation. Move the empty left arm farther clear.
Lower the recovered right egg into the front-right cup. Reorient the empty left gripper toward the loose egg behind the basket, keeping the motions separated.
Release the recovered egg in the front-right cup and withdraw vertically. Continue the left open-gripper approach toward the loose egg behind the basket.
Two eggs are visible in the holder. Withdraw the right arm and angle the left fingers forward toward the loose egg, reducing the extended vertical approach.
Replan from the interrupted pose: lift clear of the basket rim and apply smaller forward-tilt increments, while continuing the right-arm retreat.
Lower the left gripper along a forward-angled approach toward the loose rear egg, avoiding the basket rim; park the right arm clear.
Fine descent toward the loose egg with the left jaws open, holding orientation fixed and making only a small forward correction.
Close around the centered loose egg without changing wrist orientation, then perform a short vertical lift to verify retention.
The loose egg is visibly retained. Lift clear of the rim and start the transfer toward the empty front-left cup without rotating the grasp.
Translate the retained egg above the front-left socket while preserving the grasp orientation and keeping the left wrist on its side of center.
Lower the held egg toward the front-left cup with a small lateral centering correction, preserving the stable grasp orientation.
Seat the third egg with a short controlled descent, open the left gripper over the front-left cup, and begin a small withdrawal.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward to verify the third placement, then move back toward the final basket egg and begin setting an inward-angled grasp.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Position the left gripper over the final basket egg with its inward angle established before grasping.
Center the final egg between the open left jaws and lower along the pre-set angle, keeping the right arm parked.
The front rim is restricting the approach. Shift slightly inward with small steps, close around the final egg, then make a short retention-test lift.
The final egg is still in the basket and the angled approach is obstructed. Lift free and reset toward a more vertical grasp before descending again.
The previous request executed nothing. Use a small vertical withdrawal first, then very small wrist corrections to preserve joint continuity.
Move above the final egg and open only after gaining rim clearance, continuing a gradual reset toward a vertical grasp.
Descend nearly vertically over the last basket egg, keeping the open fingers centered and the wrist orientation fixed.
Fine-center the final egg between the fingers, close the left gripper, and make a small straight lift to test retention without rotating.
Lift the final egg clear of the basket with the left grip closed; introduce only small inward wrist increments while monitoring retention.
Carry the retained final egg toward the remaining cup, gradually setting an inward and frontward approach while the right arm stays clear.
Move above the remaining back-right cup with the left wrist remaining left of center. Preserve the grasp orientation and begin only a shallow descent.
Descend over the last empty cup, keeping the final egg retained and correcting its lateral alignment by only a few millimeters.
The final egg is aligned over the remaining cup, but the lid limits descent. Open to settle it into the socket, then withdraw upward and left to verify all four placements.
All four eggs are visibly in their cups. Clear the left arm and bring the closed right gripper above the lid for a controlled closing push.
Approach the upper rear edge of the lid with the closed right fingertips. Move the left arm toward its home area while retaining its elbow-up configuration.
Contact the lid's upper edge with the closed right gripper and sweep gently toward the front and downward. Continue returning the left arm toward home.
The lid is nearly closed. Apply a short downward seating motion with the right fingertips while completing the left arm's return toward origin.
The lid appears fully seated. Lift the right fingers clear before opening, then begin a gradual return toward home; settle the left arm at origin.
The closed lid remains stable. Continue returning the right arm toward its original pose with smooth translation and wrist rotation, keeping both grippers open.
